**The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** is a strong pick for either appliance. Its **2,600 W AC output** is enough for a typical single-burner induction cooktop rated up to 1,800 W, with some headroom, and its **2,073.6 Wh battery** gives you useful cooking or boiling capacity. [Product details and buying link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)

For perspective, a 1,800 W cooktop running continuously would use the battery in roughly an hour after losses; normal cooking may last longer if you turn the heat down. A litre of water takes roughly 90–110 Wh to boil, so check your kettle’s label and treat boil-count estimates as approximate. [Cooktop power and runtime guidance](https://powerstationmatch.com/devices/induction-cooktop) · [Kettle and boil estimates](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop)
